title: Energy, Work and Power Module 6 Lesson 1: Connected Particles Energy custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Two particles $A$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ and $B$ of mass $5\text{ kg}$ are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a small smooth fixed pulley. The particles are released from rest with both strings vertical. Calculate their speed after each has moved a distance of $1.6\text{ m}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A particle $P$ of mass $4\text{ kg}$ is on a smooth horizontal table and connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to a hanging particle $Q$ of mass $1\text{ kg}$. The system is released from rest. Find the speed of the particles after $Q$ has fallen $1.25\text{ m}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Particle $A$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ is on a rough horizontal table (coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.2$), connected over a smooth pulley to a hanging particle $B$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$. The system moves $0.8\text{ m}$ from rest. Calculate the total kinetic energy of the system. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Particle $A$ of mass $1\text{ kg}$ is on a smooth plane inclined at $\theta$ where $\sin\theta = 0.6$, connected over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging particle $B$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$. The system is released from rest. Find the speed of the particles after moving $0.5\text{ m}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Particle $P$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$ on a smooth $30^\circ$ incline is connected over an apex pulley to particle $Q$ of mass $1\text{ kg}$ on a smooth $45^\circ$ incline. As $P$ moves down its slope, calculate the net loss in gravitational potential energy when each particle moves $1.2\text{ m}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Particle $A$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$ on a smooth table is pulled by a hanging particle $B$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ from rest. Particle $B$ falls $0.6\text{ m}$ to the floor, at which instant the string becomes slack. Find the speed of the particles just before $B$ hits the floor. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

questions.prompt: Two particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $1.2\text{ kg}$ and $1.8\text{ kg}$ respectively, are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a small fixed smooth pulley. The particles are initially held at rest with both hanging vertically at a height of $1.5\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. The system is released from rest. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use an energy method to find the speed of $B$ at the instant it hits the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: After $B$ hits the ground, the string goes slack and $A$ continues to move vertically upwards. Find the greatest height reached by $A$ above the ground.

questions.prompt: A block $P$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$ lies on a smooth horizontal table, $2\text{ m}$ from a small smooth pulley at the edge of the table. A light inextensible string connects $P$ to a particle $Q$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$ hanging freely over the pulley. The system is released from rest with the string taut. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use conservation of mechanical energy to find the speed of the system when $Q$ has fallen a distance of $0.8\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By considering the work-energy principle applied to particle $P$ alone, determine the tension in the string during this motion.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $4\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal table. The coefficient of friction between $A$ and the table is $\mu = 0.25$. A light inextensible string connected to $A$ passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table and carries a hanging particle $B$ of mass $3\text{ kg}$. The system is released from rest with $B$ at a height of $1.2\text{ m}$ above the floor. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done against friction while $B$ falls to the floor, and use the work-energy principle to find the speed of $B$ just before impact.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: After $B$ hits the floor, $A$ continues to slide along the table with the string slack. Calculate the additional distance $A$ slides before coming to rest.

questions.prompt: Two particles $A$ and $B$, of masses $5\text{ kg}$ and $3\text{ kg}$ respectively, are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a small smooth pulley fixed at the apex of a plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Particle $A$ hangs vertically below the pulley and particle $B$ rests on the smooth incline. The particles are released from rest when the difference in their vertical heights is $1.2\text{ m}$, with $A$ being $1.2\text{ m}$ lower than $B$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: At the instant when $A$ and $B$ reach the same horizontal level, calculate the distance $x$ moved by each particle along its path.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use an energy method to find the speed of the particles at the instant they are at the same horizontal level.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ is on a rough plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. A light inextensible string connects $A$ to a particle $B$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ hanging vertically over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline. A force of $4\text{ N}$ is applied to $A$ acting down the incline. The system moves $1.5\text{ m}$ from rest, and the total work done against friction during this movement is $1.8\text{ J}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done by the applied $4\text{ N}$ force and the net change in gravitational potential energy of the system.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the work-energy principle to find the speed of the particles after moving $1.5\text{ m}$.

questions.prompt: Two particles $P$ and $Q$, of masses $0.8\text{ kg}$ and $m\text{ kg}$ respectively, are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a fixed small smooth pulley at the apex between two inclined planes. Particle $P$ rests on a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, and particle $Q$ rests on a rough plane inclined at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal. A force of $1.5\text{ N}$ acts on $P$ down its incline, causing $P$ to move down and $Q$ to be pulled up its incline. When each particle has moved $1.2\text{ m}$ from rest, their speed is $0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and the work done against friction on $Q$ is $0.72\text{ J}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy of $P$, the work done by the $1.5\text{ N}$ applied force, the potential energy lost by $P$, and the net mechanical energy delivered to particle $Q$ after accounting for friction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Express the kinetic energy gained and potential energy gained by $Q$ in terms of $m$, and use the work-energy principle to find the value of $m$ to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$ is on a plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between $A$ and the plane is $\mu = 0.15$. A light inextensible string attached to $A$ passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the incline and supports a hanging particle $B$ of mass $3.5\text{ kg}$. The system is released from rest with $B$ at a height of $1.6\text{ m}$ above the ground. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal reaction and friction force on $A$, and use the work-energy principle to find the speed of $B$ at the instant it hits the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: When $B$ hits the ground, the string becomes slack. Particle $A$ continues to move up the incline before coming to instantaneous rest. Find the further distance $A$ moves up the incline after $B$ lands, and the total distance moved by $A$ from its initial position.
